result.summary: Extracts the internal `sigterm_node` helper and Windows process group configuration into module-level functions in `feature_init.py`. It replaces `node.kill_process()` in `init_fd_overflow_test` with `sigterm_node(node)`, ensuring graceful SIGTERM shutdown instead of an abrupt kill, and replaces manual wait assertions with `node.wait_until_stopped()`.
result.problem: Terminating bitcoind via `node.kill_process()` during `init_fd_overflow_test` causes `llvm-symbolizer` broken pipe errors when resolving UBSAN suppressions during test execution in sanitized environments.
evidence: PR description: 'Fixes #36388 (llvm-symbolizer broken pipe complaints) by replacing the unclean Bitcoin Core shutdown with a clean one in init_fd_overflow_test.'

Commit message: 'Use self.sigterm_node(node)+get_process_group_kwargs() over node.kill_process() for a graceful shutdown to avoid complaints from the llvm-symbolizer about a broken pipe when it resolves UBSAN suppressions during a process kill'

result.card: This PR extracts a module-level sigterm_node helper in feature_init.py and updates init_fd_overflow_test to shut down via SIGTERM rather than node.kill_process(). Abruptly killing the process caused llvm-symbolizer broken pipe errors when resolving UBSAN suppressions in sanitized environments, tracked in issue #36388. Gracefully terminating the node avoids broken pipes while also standardizing process group flags across platforms.
